company.name: Forkful
company.description: A food delivery marketplace with 6,000 restaurants. Menus come from restaurants; Forkful adds dietary and allergen filters on top. Forkful Pass gives free delivery.

title: Forkful: a month of feedback
brief: Forkful's inbox for the last 30 days holds 66 pieces of feedback: app reviews, support tickets and NPS comments. The PM who used to triage it has left, and the team plans the next quarter on Monday. Group the feedback into themes, set the noise aside, flag anything critical, rank the themes by what matters, and write opportunities for the top ones.

themes.label: Allergen filters show unsafe dishes
themes.summary: Since a menu import change, allergen tags are dropped for some restaurants and the filters treat untagged dishes as safe. People with allergies are being served food that can put them in hospital.
themes.opportunity: How might we make sure an allergen filter never shows a dish we cannot vouch for, starting with hiding untagged dishes from filtered results today?

themes.label: The app crashes
themes.summary: Crashes in core flows. People lose work and cannot finish what they came to do.
themes.opportunity: How might we catch crashes in core flows before release, and fix the top crash signatures this sprint?

themes.label: Support is slow
themes.summary: Slow or unhelpful support. It multiplies the pain of every other problem, but it is a symptom as much as a cause.
themes.opportunity: How might we answer the most common questions before people need to contact us, and reply to the rest within a day?

themes.label: Too many notifications
themes.summary: Push and email volume annoys people. Easy to fix and worth fixing, but it does not stop anyone from using the product.
themes.opportunity: How might we let people choose which notifications they get, and send fewer that matter more?

themes.label: Upsells are pushy
themes.summary: Upgrade prompts feel aggressive. It erodes goodwill, but nobody is blocked.
themes.opportunity: How might we show Forkful Pass at the moment someone needs it, instead of on every screen?

themes.label: The price feels too high
themes.summary: Complaints about the price and the last increase. Loud and frequent, but people still use the product; it is a positioning question, not a broken experience.
themes.opportunity: How might we make the value of Forkful Pass obvious before renewal, so the price feels earned?

themes.label: Requests for scheduled weekly orders
themes.summary: A popular request. It signals what people want next, but its absence does not hurt anyone today.
themes.opportunity: How might we find out which job scheduled weekly orders would do for people, and whether a smaller version solves it?

hidden.explanation: The critical problem, "Allergen filters show unsafe dishes", appears in only 3 items, all from the last 6 days. Few items, but each describes harm that grows every day it stays live, so it goes first whatever the volume. Volume alone would put "Too many notifications" next, with 14 items, but it is a low-severity problem. "The app crashes" (9 items, high severity) and "Support is slow" (11 items, medium severity) hurt more people more. Impact here is reach times severity: low counts 1, medium 2, high 3 per item. 10 items were noise: praise, spam and off-topic messages that belong in no theme.
hidden.principle: Rank feedback by reach times severity, not by volume, and read the rare, recent and severe items first: a critical problem is usually quiet before it gets loud.
